title: Omeprazole inhibits primary active transport (H/K-ATPase)
vignette: Many drugs and toxins act by inhibiting substance flow across cell membranes. Which of the following inhibits primary active transport?

clues.text: inhibiting substance flow across cell membranes
clues.note: Membrane transport is passive (down a gradient, no ATP) or active (against a gradient, uses ATP); the question targets PRIMARY active transport (direct ATP hydrolysis by an ATPase).
Primary active transport uses an ATPase (e.g., Na/K-ATPase, H/K-ATPase, Ca-ATPase) that directly hydrolyzes ATP to move ions against their gradient - omeprazole blocks the H/K-ATPase.

whatMatters: PRIMARY active transport is carried out by ATPases that directly hydrolyze ATP to pump ions against their gradient (Na/K-, H/K-, Ca-ATPase). OMEPRAZOLE (a proton pump inhibitor) inhibits the gastric parietal-cell H/K-ATPase (proton pump), reducing acid secretion. Answer C.
strategy: Match the drug to the transport type it blocks. Omeprazole -> H/K-ATPase = PRIMARY active transport. Reject blockers of PASSIVE (channel-mediated) transport: tetrodotoxin (voltage-gated Na channels), verapamil (L-type Ca channels), lidocaine (voltage-gated Na channels), and dofetilide (delayed-rectifier K channels) - all inhibit passive ion flow, not an ATP-driven pump.

eliminations.label: Tetrodotoxin - blocks voltage-gated Na channels (passive)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a pufferfish neurotoxin that blocks voltage-gated sodium channels. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: sodium channels mediate PASSIVE transport (down the gradient), not ATP-driven primary active transport. ✅ Correct if: asking what blocks passive Na channel flow.

eliminations.label: Verapamil - blocks L-type Ca channels (passive)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it inhibits PASSIVE calcium entry through L-type channels, not a primary active ATPase. ✅ Correct if: asking about passive calcium channel blockade.

eliminations.label: Lidocaine - blocks voltage-gated Na channels (passive)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a local anesthetic / class IB antiarrhythmic. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it blocks voltage-gated sodium channels (passive transport), not an ATPase. ✅ Correct if: passive Na-channel blockade (nerve/cardiac).

eliminations.label: Dofetilide - blocks delayed-rectifier K channels (passive)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a class III antiarrhythmic that blocks the rapid delayed-rectifier potassium current. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it inhibits PASSIVE potassium efflux (prolonging repolarization/QT), not primary active transport. ✅ Correct if: passive K-channel blockade (QT prolongation).

reasoning: Primary active transport uses ATPases that directly hydrolyze ATP to move ions against a gradient
Omeprazole inhibits the gastric parietal-cell H/K-ATPase (proton pump)
Blocking this ATPase reduces gastric acid secretion
-> omeprazole; answer C (the others block passive ion channels)
mechanism: Transport across cell membranes is either PASSIVE (movement DOWN an electrochemical gradient through channels or carriers, requiring no energy) or ACTIVE (movement AGAINST a gradient, requiring energy). PRIMARY active transport is performed by ATPase 'pumps' that DIRECTLY hydrolyze ATP - classic examples are the Na/K-ATPase, the Ca-ATPase, and the gastric H/K-ATPase (the parietal-cell 'proton pump' that exchanges luminal K+ for H+ to acidify the stomach). OMEPRAZOLE and other proton pump inhibitors irreversibly inhibit the H/K-ATPase, decreasing gastric acid (used for peptic ulcer disease, GERD, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome) - so omeprazole inhibits a primary active transporter. The distractors all block PASSIVE (channel-mediated) transport that flows down the gradient without ATP: tetrodotoxin and lidocaine block voltage-gated Na+ channels, verapamil blocks L-type Ca2+ channels, and dofetilide blocks delayed-rectifier K+ channels. (Secondary active transport - e.g., the Na-glucose cotransporter - uses the gradient set up by a primary pump, not direct ATP hydrolysis.)

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Physio/Pharm > primary active transport = ATPase pumps (Na/K-, H/K-, Ca-ATPase) hydrolyze ATP; omeprazole (PPI) inhibits gastric H/K-ATPase; passive transport = channels (Na, Ca, K).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Primary active transport = ATP-hydrolyzing pump; omeprazole blocks the H/K-ATPase.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on primary vs secondary active transport, passive transport, ATPase, or proton pump? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Tetrodotoxin/lidocaine (Na channels), verapamil (Ca channels), dofetilide (K channels) all block PASSIVE channel flow.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: omeprazole inhibits H/K-ATPase (primary active transport); channel blockers act on passive transport.

keywords.front: Drug that inhibits primary active transport

keywords.back: Uses gradient from a primary pump (e.g., Na-glucose cotransporter)

memoryHook: Only the proton pump (H/K-ATPase) burns ATP to push ions uphill - omeprazole jams it; the other drugs just plug passive channels flowing downhill.
